NTI - National Telecommunication Institute
National Telecommunication Institute
The National Telecommunication Institute (NTI), established in
1983, excels in Egypt's education, research, and technical
consultation. Aligned with the Ministry of Telecommunication and
Information Technology (MCIT), NTI recognizes ICT's crucial role
in the Egyptian societal advancement. It plays a key role in
Egypt's Vision 2030 for digital transformation, supported by the
government and industry collaboration. NTI prioritizes
high-quality education, training, and innovative research,
offering consultancy and technical services.

title: NTI Scientific Departments
text:
NTI - National Telecommunication Institute
Scientific Departments
NTI consists of five scientific departments which have a group of
experts and scientists.
Network Planning Department
The Network Planning department plays a critical role in
ensuring the efficient and reliable operation of a
telecommunication networks.
Some of the key activities that a Network Planning
department undertake:
Network Design and Optimization
Capacity Planning, Network topology design, Resource
allocation, and Technology selection.
Network Deployment
Planning and arranging for the installation of new
network infrastructure.
Making certain that new hardware is compatible with
current networks.
Validating and testing newly deployed networks.
Safety Monitoring and Performance Management
Regularly keeping a close watch on network performance
and seeing possible issues, taking remedial measures to
address problems with network performance, Reporting to
regulating authorities and operators on network safety
measures, and Ensuring compliance with all relevant
regulations and standards.
Network Security
Recognizing and evaluating threats to network security.
Creating and carrying out security guidelines and
protocols.
Compliance and Regulatory Affairs
Ensuring compliance with all relevant regulations and
standards and Preparing reports and documentation for
regulatory agencies.
The Department has academic members who work in several
research fields such as:
Design and evaluate the performance of computer networks.
Wireless and mobile networks security planning and
optimization.
Wireless and mobile networks security.
Green communication networks.
Cloud computing.
Cognitive Radio.
For more information, you can contact
NetworkDept@nti.sci.eg
Computers and Systems Department
The Computers and Systems Department is interested in
everything new in many computer areas related to information
technology, including multiple operating systems, whether
Windows Server or Linux, computer programming and
applications, typical and modern computer networks and their
security, building cloud computing and virtual systems, as
well as programming modern networks and their applications,
whether automatic control using Software-defined programming
or artificial intelligence.
The department provides the consultation and training for
both the graduate and the undergraduate engineers in these
fields.
The Computers and Systems Department acting on:
Academic, applied and practical training in the fields of
cloud computing, data security, networks, various
operating systems, artificial intelligence and data
analysis.
Supervising, operating and maintaining the institute’s
networks in its various branches.
Follow up on diploma server services and exam work on the
LMS.
The Department has academic members who work in several
research fields such as:
Cloud Computing.
Machine learning, artificial intelligence and data mining.
Multimedia Communication.
Information Security.
Internet of Things (IoT).
Smart cites & their applications.
For more information, you can contact
computer_dept@nti.sci.eg
Electronics Department
The Department of Electronics focuses on applied and
scientific research in the field of design and engineering
of communications electronics. The department supports and
cooperates with the local industry and provides high-level
training programs in the field of electronics design, such
as embedded systems, integrated circuit design (IC. Design)
, and printed circuits board (PCB), in addition to assistive
technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the
Internet of Things (IoT). The department plays a pivotal
role in the country in designing and manufacturing printed
circuits board with single/double layers with high quality
through Printed circuits laboratory. The department plays
important role in the field of Robotics.
Electronics Department acting on:
Design, manufacture and measurement of printed electronic
circuits.
Design, program, test and develop the tracking device.
The Department has academic members who work in several
research fields such as:
Integrated Circuit Design (IC design).
Printed Circuit Board (PCB).
Embedded systems.
Artificial Intelligence (AI).
Internet of things (IoT).
For more information, you can contact
Electronics.Dept@nti.sci.eg
Transmission Department
The department's interests focus on transmission systems and
transmission technologies. It offers continuous education
and professional training for telecommunication engineers
especially in the optical and microwave communication
domains. The department also offers consultation for
companies operating microwave and optical systems.
The department has several laboratories for practical
training: FTTx lab equipped with all necessary equipment and
tools for field planning and testing, AirPON lab
demonstrating FTTH solution for congested areas with
complete distribution network configuration; digital
communication lab offering fundamental training for
telecommunication engineers equipped with PDH and SDH
testing equipment.
Transmission Department acting on:
Training in the field of planning, implementation,
operation, and testing of optical fiber networks.
Implementing special courses for some government agencies
and private companies in the field of fiber systems and
microwave systems
Offers consultations in the field of telecommunications
systems using optical fibers and radio telecommunications
systems,
The Department has academic members who work in several
research fields such as:
6G Reconfigurable intelligent surface.
TeraHertz communication and sensing.
AI in 6G and MIMO antenna.
For more information, you can contact
Transmission.Dept@nti.sci.eg
Switching and Traffic Department
The Switching and Traffic department studies
telecommunications networks and systems. The department’s
faculty and engineers actively participate in the areas of
research, consultancy and training.
The department offers consultancy services covering a range
of telecommunications aspects like data and voice networks,
unified communications, and converged infrastructure. The
consultancy process involves:
Assessing the client's current systems, networks,
hardware, software, and integration capabilities,
alongside evaluating organizational needs, user
requirements, budget constraints, and future expansion
plans.
Evaluating and recommending technologies, solutions, and
vendors based on client needs.
Designing and implementing customized solutions to align
with client goals and technical requirements, with
assistance provided in implementation planning, vendor
selection, and project management for smooth deployment.
Monitoring and optimizing performance along with risk
management and security measures implementation to ensure
the protection of client networks against various threats.
Training on new technologies is offered if required.
The department encompasses comprehensive curricula designed
to equip individuals with the knowledge, skills, and
competencies required to excel in various roles within the
industry.
The Department has academic members who work in several
research fields such as:
Telecommunications Networks Signaling.
VoIP and Beyond.
Network and Data Security (Cyber Security).
Internet of Things (IoT).
Artificial Intelligent (AI) and Machine Learning (ML).
Machine Unlearning.
Smart Utilities.
Vehicular Communications.
Intelligent Reflective Surface (IRS) in Cellular
Communications.
Augmented Reality (AR).
For more information, you can contact
SwitchingDepartment@nti.sci.eg

title: NTI Digital Egypt Youth - Specialized Upskilling Programs
text:
NTI - National Telecommunication Institute
Capacity Building - DEY - Upskilling Programs
Digital Egypt Youth (DEY) – Upskilling Programs
These programs are designed to foster employability rates and
empower the Egyptian community by establishing a comprehensive,
practical, and high-quality learning ecosystem. Focused on the
learner, this program leverages distinctive content crafted by
NTI in collaboration with industry main players. With an annual
goal of training and qualifying approximately 8,000
participants, including students and graduates from Egyptian
universities, candidates undergo 60,72,120 hours of technical
modules and soft skills courses to align their knowledge with
market demands.
About the initiative
About the Initiative
The success of any sector is highly dependent on
the efficiency, professionalism, and experience of
its human resources. Recognizing globally that
youth are the future workforce representing the
strategies of different nations for advancement
across government, business, and private sectors
at all professional levels, there has been a
widespread interest in equipping them with the
necessary skills to enhance performance and
achieve planned outcomes.
Therefore, the National Telecommunications
Institute places a significant emphasis on
elevating the competency and qualification of
youth at all levels. Leveraging its expertise,
resources, and partnerships with major global
companies and international organizations, the
Institute serves this vital and crucial sector.
To address the evolving needs of the workforce in
the field of telecommunications and information
technology, especially considering the constraints
of work or study, the National Telecommunications
Institute launched the "Digital Egypt Youth
Evening" initiative. This initiative aims to build
the capabilities of the workforce in these fields,
providing training on the latest technologies
while accommodating the schedules of those unable
to commit to full-time training, such as students,
graduates, or working professionals in the
telecommunications and information technology
sector.
Given the continuous development in various
applications and aspects of modern life, and the
state's commitment to digitizing all services, the
National Telecommunications Institute plays a
national role in developing and enhancing the
skills of workers in this vital sector or those
newly joining the workforce. The evening
initiative methodology combines technological
skill development, practical experience, and
qualification for obtaining specialized
international certifications.
Training within the "Digital Egypt Youth Evening"
initiative follows a high-quality integrated
system that links scientific knowledge with
practical experiences according to the current
needs of the job market. The program primarily
targets those already working in the field of
communications and information technology,
offering the flexibility to attend either through
interactive online lectures or physically at the
Institute's premises and regional branches across
various governorates.
Close
Tracks Details
Terms and Conditions
Terms and General Regulations Governing the
Initiative
Admission Requirements:
Egyptian nationality.
Holder of a relevant qualification or a
student in the final years of an Egyptian
university.
Passing admission tests.
Commitment to achieving a minimum attendance
rate of 75% of the total training hours.
Required Documents for Admission:
Copy of the national ID card.
Graduation certificate copy (for graduates).
Certificate of enrollment for the academic
year or student ID card for the current
academic year (for final-year students).
Two personal photos.
Declaration of commitment to scholarship
conditions (a separate declaration for each
training module).
Benefits:
100% funding of training costs.
Certificate from the National
Telecommunications Institute upon successful
completion of the training program.
Academic certificates from international
companies that qualify for international
technical certifications.
For further information, you can contact:
deyevening@nti.sci.eg
Close
FAQ
Frequently Asked Questions
Q1: Who is eligible to apply for the offered
scholarship?
A1: Individuals eligible to apply for the
scholarship must possess a suitable
qualification or be in their final years at one
of the Egyptian universities. Additionally, each
specialization has specific requirements that
can be reviewed.
Q2: Does the study require attendance at the
institute's premises?
A2: The training for the Digital Egypt Youth
Scholarship Evening Program can be conducted
through one of the following methods:
Online via the internet using Interactive
Live Sessions (for applicants from all
governorates).
In-person at one of the National
Telecommunications Institute headquarters or
regional branches in the innovation centers
across various governorates.
Q3: How can students communicate with
instructors during online classes?
A3: Online classes involve live interactive
sessions between the instructor and
participants. The training is conducted through
real-time interactive lectures, fostering
complete interaction and participation between
the instructor and students.
Q4: Is there practical training, or is the study
purely theoretical?
A4: The study encompasses both theoretical and
practical aspects. Practical training is
conducted based on the content covered in the
training unit, utilizing the latest tools and
dedicated programs for this purpose.
Q5: Are working individuals allowed to enroll in
the scholarship program?
A5: The evening scholarship allows graduates who
are employed to attend, aiming to enhance their
skills. It is also open to non-full-time
students.
Q6: What is the duration of the training unit?
A6: The various training modules offer multiple
courses, each taught over a period of 12 hours
per week.
Q7: Am I allowed to enroll in more than one
training unit?
A7: Registration is permitted for one training
unit only within the same period.
Q8: Is there a mandatory order for attending the
training units?
A8: The sequencing of units depends on the
requirements of each unit and specialization. It
is essential to review the conditions of each
training unit and fulfill the requirements and
skills necessary for participation in the
training courses.
Q9: Is it necessary to enroll in units from the
same training axis?
A9: It is possible to enroll in units from
different training programs, taking into
consideration the conditions of each training
unit.
Q10: If I enroll in a new training unit within
the same training axis, do I need to retake the
admission test?
A10: Each training unit has its own conditions
and an admission test, even if it belongs to the
same training axis.
Q11: Do I receive a certificate for each
training unit, or is it one certificate for the
entire training axis?
A11: A separate attendance certificate is issued
for each training unit, encompassing the
trainee's assessment during that specific
training unit.
Q12: Can I enroll in only one training unit?
A12: Yes, you can enroll in a single training
unit.
Q13: Do I need a computer to enroll in the
scholarship?
A13: If you are studying online, it is necessary
to use a computer with suitable capabilities for
the training unit you are joining. Ensure the
availability of appropriate internet
connectivity.
Q14: When is the registration for the
scholarship opened?
A14: Registration is announced when the
available training units are ready for
enrollment.
Q15: When will I be contacted for the personal
interview?
A15: An email will be sent with the date and
time of the personal interview within two weeks
of the registration deadline.
Q16: When will I be notified of the results of
the personal interview?
A16: In the case of acceptance and completion of
the required number of participants, you will be
contacted either by phone or through email to
confirm the completion of paperwork and your
readiness to participate.
Q17: What should I do if I forget the password?
A17: There is no password or username. Access to
your personal account is done by entering your
email and national ID only.
Q18: What should I do if I entered incorrect
information during registration and want to
correct it?
A18: Send an email to
training.department@nti.sci.eg with your full
name and national ID number to request the
necessary corrections.
Q19: When is an applicant considered accepted
into the scholarship?
A19: Acceptance into the scholarship program
involves several stages:
Fulfillment of all the requirements for
enrollment in the training unit, as listed
on the registration page.
Completion of the personal interview.
Submission of all required documents.
Q20: When are the certificates issued?
A20: Certificates are issued within a month
after the completion of the training unit and
are sent via email.
Q21: How can one decline the scholarship?
A21: To decline the scholarship, send a
withdrawal request at least 48 hours before the
training start date. Include your full name,
national ID, the training unit applied for, and
the registration number in the email sent to
training.department@nti.sci.eg.
Q22: If the training schedule is inconvenient,
and a deferral is needed, what is the process?
A22: Submit a deferral request at least 48 hours
before the training start date. Include your
full name, national ID, the training unit
applied for, and the registration number in the
email sent to training.department@nti.sci.eg.
Please note that the applicant will be placed on
the waiting list.
Q23: How can I inquire about the details of the
scientific material in any training unit?
A23: Details and content of the scientific
material for the training units are available on
the website
www.nti.sci.eg/dey
Q24: Can non-Egyptian nationalities enroll in
the scholarship?
A24: The scholarship is only available for
Egyptians.
Q25: When I try to register on the website, I
get the following message: "Sorry, Invalid
registration process; your registration form is
rejected, as you registered before. for more
information, please contact us."
A25: This message indicates that you have
already registered for an account on the
institute's website, and there is no need to
create a new account. You can log in to your
existing account by entering your email and
national ID through the login page:
https://www.nti.sci.eg/dey/signin.php
Close

title: NTI Egyptian Talents Academy (ETA)
text:
NTI - National Telecommunication Institute
NTI-Huawei Egyptian Talents Academy (ETA)
NTI-Huawei Egyptian Talents Academy (ETA)
Building digital talents is one of the ICT sector's strategic
objectives to fulfill Egypt’s Vision 2030 toward a digital
society. NTI and Huawei Egypt are collaborating in establishing
the Egyptian Talents Academy (ETA).
This Academy aims to build the capabilities and digital
competencies of students and university graduates in Huawei’s
training programs in advanced technology specializations through
cooperation and partnership with specialized international
companies to expand the base of trained communications and
information technology personnel in all Egypt governorates.
ET Academy focuses on enhancing youth's competitive capabilities
in line with the local and global labor market demands by
offering training in several technological specializations in
NTI branches and its Creativa Innovation Hubs in almost all
Egyptian governorates to hone their skills and to train and
empower talented Egyptians starting with the basics and moving
on to associate, professional, and expert levels.
ETA will spearhead a transformative shift in Egypt's ICT
landscape, ensuring Egypt's competitive edge in the digital
economy by harnessing industry-leading expertise and
state-of-the-art infrastructure. The primary objective is
cultivating a highly skilled workforce proficient in
next-generation ICT technologies. A variety of disciplines will
be covered in comprehensive training modules, including but not
limited to data network (Datacom), security, fifth generation
(5G), artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data, etc.
About
the initiative
Courses
Courses by Governorate
Terms
and Conditions
FAQ
About the initiative
The National Telecommunication Institute (NTI) and
Huawei are cooperating under the auspices of the
Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
(MCIT) to launch the Egyptian Talents Academy program,
to provide training to Egyptian youth.
ETA represents a visionary effort to train and empower
tech talents from associates to experts, via NTI
branches and creativa innovation hubs spread across
all Egyptian governorates.
The primary objective is to cultivate a highly skilled
workforce proficient in next-generation ICT
technologies. A variety of disciplines will be covered
in comprehensive training modules, including but not
limited to datacom, security, 5G, artificial
intelligence, cloud, big data, etc.
ETA will spearhead a transformative shift in Egypt's
ICT landscape, ensuring Egypt's competitive edge in
the digital economy by harnessing industry-leading
expertise and state-of-the-art infrastructure.
The selected candidates will gain the knowledge and
skills needed to succeed at the expert level in your
favorite track, starting with the basics and moving on
to HCIA, HCIP, and HCIE.
Close
Terms and General Regulations Governing the
Initiative
Enrollment Requirements:
The applicant must be an Egyptian national.
The applicant must have a suitable educational qualification or be a final-year student.
Fulfill the basic prerequisites for each training track.
Submit the required documents for enrollment in the program.
Pass the admission tests.
Required Documents Upon Acceptance:
A copy of the national ID card.
A copy of the graduation certificate for graduates.
An enrollment certificate or university ID card showing the academic year the student is enrolled in.
One personal photo.
A commitment statement to adhere to the scholarship conditions, to be downloaded and uploaded through the program's website.
General Rules of the Academy:
Each applicant must create a personal account on the Academy's website to upload all required documents.
Ensure the accuracy of all information recorded in the commitment statement.
Adhere to the required number of hours for each training program.
Maintain an attendance rate of no less than 80% of the total hours of the program.
Demonstrate appropriate behavior when interacting with trainers and organizers of the Academy.
Complete the program and pass the required exams to receive the attendance and course completion certificates.
Preserve the course materials and refrain from publishing them online (intellectual property rights).
Submit a new signed commitment statement for each training course the trainee enrolls in.
Submit or send a withdrawal notice via email at least 48 hours before the start of the training program.
All correspondence must be conducted through the official Academy email:
ETA@nti.sci.eg
.
Close
Frequently Asked Questions
If the answer to your inquiry is not available
through the frequently asked questions, you can send
your inquiry via email to
ETA@nti.sci.eg
.
Q1: Who is eligible to apply for the offered
scholarship?
A1: Those who hold appropriate qualifications or
final-year students at an Egyptian university,
provided they meet the specific requirements for
each training specialization as announced on the
website.
Q2: Does the study require attendance at the
institute's premises?
A2: The training takes place at the premises of the
National Telecommunications Institute or at the
creativa centers in various governorates of Egypt.
Q3 - Is there practical training or is the study
only theoretical?
A3 - The study includes both theoretical and
practical aspects. Practical training is provided
according to the content of the training unit using
the latest means and specialized programs.
Q4 - What is the duration of the training unit?
A4 - Various training modules offer multiple
courses. The duration of the first-level units is a
minimum of 70 study hours and increases according to
the training level enrolled in.
Q5 - Are employees allowed to join the scholarship?
A5 - Advanced levels, which enable the trainee to
obtain an expert degree, are allowed for employees
to improve their efficiency.
Q6 - Am I allowed to enroll in more than one
training unit?
A6 - To ensure specialization and efficiency
improvement, enrollment is allowed in only one
training unit at a time.
Q7 - Is there a mandatory sequence for attending
units?
A7 - The sequence of units depends on the
requirements and specialization of each unit. You
must review the conditions of each training unit and
meet the necessary prerequisites and skills for
enrollment in the training courses.
Q8 - If I enroll in a new training unit within the
same training track, do I need to pass the admission
test again?
A8 - Each training unit has its own conditions and
admission test, even if it's within the same
training track.
Q9 - Do I receive a certificate for each training
unit, or is it one certificate for the entire
training track?
A9 - A certificate of attendance is issued for each
training unit separately, including the trainee's
evaluation during that unit.
Q10 - How can I inquire about the scientific content
of any training unit?
A10 - Details and content of the scientific material
for the training units are available on the
institute's website:
www.nti.sci.eg
Q11 - Can non-Egyptian nationals enroll in the
scholarship?
A11 - The scholarship is for Egyptians only.
Q12 - When will I be contacted for the personal
interview?
A12 - An email will be sent with the date and time
of the personal interview within two weeks of the
registration closing date.
Q13 - When will I be notified of the personal
interview result?
A13 - If accepted, you will be contacted by phone or
email to confirm the submission of the necessary
documents for enrollment in the training unit.
Q14 - What should I do if I made an error in my
registration details and need to correct it?
A14 - Send an email to ETA @nti.sci.eg with your
full name and national ID number.
Q15 - When is an applicant considered accepted for
the scholarship?
A15 - Acceptance for the scholarship has several
stages:
Meeting all the conditions for enrollment in the
training unit, as listed on the registration
page.
Completing the personal interview.
Submitting all required documents.
Q16 - When are certificates issued?
A16 - Certificates are issued within a month of
completing the training unit and sent via email.
Q17 - How do I withdraw from the scholarship?
A17 - Send a withdrawal request at least 48 hours
before the start date of the training, including
your full name, national ID number, the training
unit you applied for, and the registration number to
ETA@nti.sci.eg
.
Q18 - The training schedule is not suitable, and I
need to defer?
A18 - Send a deferral request at least 48 hours
before the start date of the training, including
your full name, national ID number, the training
unit you applied for, and the registration number to
ETA@nti.sci.eg
.
Note that the applicant will be placed on the
waiting list.
Close

Capacity Building - NTI's Private Summer Training Program
NTI's Private Summer Training Program
Step into the future of technology and innovation with NTI's Private Summer Training Program, designed to equip students with the skills and knowledge needed to excel in today's dynamic job market. This comprehensive 4-week program delivers
120 hours of immersive training
, including
30 hours of essential labor market skills (Soft Skills)
and
90 hours of advanced technical training
tailored to align with international certification standards.
Our program spans a wide array of cutting-edge fields such as
Networks, Security, Artificial Intelligence, Cloud Computing, Web Design and Development, Graphic Design, 5G, Data Analysis, Big Data, Embedded Systems, and IoT Applications.
Each course is carefully crafted to provide practical, hands-on learning experiences that prepare you for real-world challenges.
What sets us apart is our flexibility and customization. Recognizing the unique needs of different universities, we offer tailored training programs that address specific requirements, ensuring that your education aligns perfectly with your aspirations and institutional goals.
To streamline your learning journey, we’ve categorized the training into six specialized tracks:
Telecom Engineering
Focused on communication systems and advanced telecom technologies.
System Engineering
Covering system architecture and integration techniques.
Software Engineering
Emphasizing software development, algorithms, and design.
Network Engineering
Training in advanced networking and cybersecurity protocols.
Data Engineering
Enabling expertise in data analysis, management, and big data solutions.
Electronics and Embedded Systems
A deep dive into digital design, microcontrollers, and IoT.
Join us for a transformative experience that not only prepares you for the competitive global job market but also positions you as a leader in the ever-evolving world of technology.

Capacity Building - NTI's Private Summer Training Program
NTI's Private Summer Training Program
This comprehensive 4-week program offers a total of 120 hours of immersive and structured training, designed to equip participants with the skills needed to excel in today’s competitive job market. The program includes:
30 hours dedicated to essential labor market skills,
such as communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and other critical soft skills that enhance workplace readiness.
90 hours of in-depth, advanced technical training,
meticulously crafted to meet international certification standards.
Part 1: Personal Skills - (Soft Skills or Freelancing Skills) (30 Hours).
Soft Skills
General Skills:
General soft skills that you need to establish the culture of soft skills in your employees such as:
Communication Skills
Learning how to communicate with people outside of the field, such as clients and sometimes the general public, who do not have a technical background.
Interview skills
When fresh graduate or under graduate can present himself with ease, he can have a much higher chance of getting the job that he wants.
Presentation skills
It empowers presenters to raise their delivery to the next level of professional communication and learn to create and deliver powerful, persuasive and memorable presentations.
Leadership Skills:
Leadership soft skills that you need to teach your employees to help them become more efficient executives and better team managers in the future like:
Teamwork skills

title: NTI HireReady Initiative
text:
NTI - National Telecommunication Institute
Capacity Building - DEY - HireReady
Digital Egypt Youth (DEY) – HireReady Initiative.
The Digital Egypt Youth (DEY) initiative plays a vital role in achieving one of the strategic objectives of the ICT sector by empowering young Egyptians to thrive in the digital economy, contributing to the country’s socioeconomic development and digital transformation initiatives.
The Digital Egypt Youth (DEY) initiative aims to provide young Egyptians with the necessary skills and knowledge to thrive in the digital age. The initiative focuses on training youth in various digital fields to increase their employability and entrepreneurship opportunities. The initiative aims to bridge the digital skills gap in Egypt and create a digitally skilled workforce to support the country’s digital transformation. It specifically targets young Egyptians, equipping them with in-demand skills needed for jobs in the digital economy.
The initiative offers a full-fledged scholarship and targets 2500 fresh graduates from Egyptian universities nationwide. The initiative adopts the upskilling approach: technical up-skilling and personal and soft skills up-skilling aspects. The program seeks to cover various digital skills to cater to diverse interests and career paths.
The Digital Egypt Youth (DEY) initiative collaborates with industry partners and experts to develop and deliver relevant training content. This ensures that the program aligns with industry requirements and equips participants with practical skills and knowledge that are in demand in the job market. The program aims to facilitate job placement for trained participants by partnering with industry stakeholders and creating linkages between trained individuals and potential employers through one month of job training at the industry partner premises. This helps connect young talent with job opportunities in the digital sector. NTI collaborated with more than 75 national and multinational industry partners including but not limited to, Amazon, Etisalat Egypt, Vodafone, Huawei, WE, Cisco, VMware, Orange, Valeo, Avelabs, and SEITech, Brightsky, VOIS to design more than 30 professional tracks to meet job profiles and ICT market need. At the end of the program, participants receive certification that validate their skills and competencies. Theses certificates help enhance their employability and serve as credentials for future job opportunities.
A key target field of the Digital Egypt Initiative is the electronics & embedded systems to match the presidential initiative HireReady.

About the initiative
The initiative is offered as a full-fledged scholarship for selected fresh Egyptian university graduates within five calendar years of their graduation. It helps in bridging the gap between the talent skills and the regional and international market need. Collaboration with more than 75 national and multinational industry partners and more than 30 professional tracks. Candidates will join after a fine screening process done in cooperation with our industry partners. Tracks are designed in cooperation with our industry partners to meet job profiles and ICT market needs. Each track has a duration of four months including technical program, soft skills program, in addition to a one month on job training at the industry partner premises. After passing the track the candidates will receive joint certificates from NTI and our industry partners.
Our close cooperation with our industry partners helps securing the employment of the top qualified training candidates.

Terms and General Regulations Governing the Initiative
Commitment to submit all required documents on the
initiative's electronic platform upon approval of these
terms and regulations is a fundamental requirement for
scholarship acceptance:
Copy of the graduation certificate.
Scanned copy of the national ID card.
Signed declaration by the trainee.
Compliance with the fundamental requirements of each
training program is a prerequisite for acceptance into the
scholarship.
Commitment to the scheduled training hours (7 training hours
daily).
Adherence to the prescribed attendance percentage of not
less than 75%.
Commitment to appropriate behavior and professional
etiquette with everyone during the training period within
the initiative.
Commitment to preserving academic materials and refraining
from posting them on electronic platforms (intellectual
property rights).
Commitment to the accuracy of all information stated in the
declaration.
Commitment to submitting a new signed declaration for each
training course the trainee enrolls in.
Commitment to providing a notification or sending an apology
via email for non-completion of the scholarship, at least 48
hours before the commencement of the training.
Only communications through the official email of the
initiative (D4m@nti.sci.eg) will be considered.

Frequently Asked Questions
1. Who is eligible to apply for the scholarship?
The initiative allows anyone who has not graduated more than
five years ago to apply.
2. Does studying require attending the institute's premises?
Yes, the initiative is available through the attendance
system at the institute's locations.
3. Is there practical training or is the study purely
theoretical?
The study includes both theoretical and practical aspects,
and practical training is conducted based on the content
covered in the training unit using the latest methods and
specialized programs.
4. Are employees allowed to join the scholarship?
To be eligible for the scholarship, full commitment to
attending lectures on a daily basis throughout the training
unit is required.
5. What is the duration of the training unit?
The training unit lasts for 3 months at the institute's
premises, in addition to one month of practical training at
one of the companies supporting the selected training unit.
6. If I have previously benefited from the scholarships offered by the institute (6-month scholarship or 3-month scholarship), am I eligible to apply for the new training units?
You can only benefit from the "HireReady" and "Digital Egypt Youth" initiatives once.
7. Do I need a computer to join the scholarship?
It is preferable to have a personal computer (laptop) to
maximize the program's benefits. If that is not possible,
the National Telecommunications Institute will provide you
with a computer throughout the training period at the
premises.
8. When will I be contacted for the interview?
Once the application period is closed, you will be contacted
to schedule the acceptance tests, which will require your
presence at the premises on the specified date.
9. When will I be notified of the interview results?
The results will be announced within two weeks after the
interview. If you are accepted and the required number of
participants is complete, you will be contacted to confirm
the completion of paperwork and your readiness to
participate.
10. What should I do if I entered incorrect information in
the registration form and want to correct it?
Send an email to
D4m@nti.sci.eg
with your
full name and national ID number, and follow-up will be
done.
11. How can I change my preferences?
Send an email to
D4m@nti.sci.eg
with your
full name and national ID number, requesting the deletion of
all preferences. After that, you can enter new preferences
using the same personal account. Please note that
modifications will be treated as a new registration starting
from the date of the modifications.
12. When is an applicant considered accepted for the
scholarship?
Acceptance into the scholarship has several stages:
First: Meeting all the requirements for joining the
training unit, as listed on the registration page.
Second: Completing the personal interview.
Third: Submitting all the required documents.
13. How can I withdraw from the scholarship?
Send a request to withdraw at least 48 hours before the
start of the training, including your full name, national ID
number, the training unit you applied for, and the
registration number, to the email address
D4m@nti.sci.eg.
14. Can non-Egyptian nationals apply for the scholarship?
The scholarship is only available for Egyptians.
15. Can you provide details about the 4-month scholarship,
such as attendance requirements, duration, and whether it is
online or offline?
The initiative follows a 5-day work system per week, with 7
working hours per day. The training sessions are held in the
morning, and attendance is required at the institute's
premises throughout the initiative period. The institute
also provides suitable transportation (free of charge) from
anywhere in Cairo to the premises during the initiative.
16. What is the deadline for submitting the certificate?
The deadline is before the start of the acceptance test
phase.
17. Will financial incentives be provided during the
training period?
Yes, a monthly allowance will be provided throughout the
training period at the premises (3 months).
18. Does the scholarship require a specific GPA?
The scholarship does not require a specific GPA. It only
requires selecting one of the eligible specialties and
passing the acceptance tests.
Close

title: NTI Wazeefa-Tech Initiative
text:
NTI - National Telecommunication Institute
Wazeefa-Tech Initiative
This presidential initiative is categorized under the
train-to-hire programs strategy of MCIT. The philosophy here is
how to change the traditional model of training and skill
development perception. The objective of this initiative is to
encourage the candidate to invest in his/her future and get a
job at the end of the program. During the journey of training
the candidates acquired specific technologies based on the ICT
companies’ needs and requirements to ensure that candidates are
prepared to contribute effectively upon hire. The cost of
training varies according to the specializations with no
additional expenses. All extra expenses will be paid by MCIT and
Tahya Misr Fund. Thus, the trainees will pay only the cost of
the training after being employed. Nasr Social Bank will cover
the cost of the training with a zero-interest loan. Once the
trainee lands a job, he/she can repay the loan from their
salaries which not be less than 6000EGP, in installments payable
up to three years. The advantage here is increased employability
for candidates by not only demonstrating their dedication to
gaining relevant skills but also by providing them with the
necessary qualifications and experience sought by employers. The
hiring rate of this initiative is 95% through our successful
partners locally or regionally in the field of ICT, who have
different educational backgrounds and graduated from different
universities.

title: ICT Minister Attends Graduation Ceremony of NTI Cybersecurity Academy First Cohort
text:
NTI - National Telecommunication Institute
Latest News
ICT Minister Attends Graduation Ceremony of NTI Cybersecurity Academy First Cohort
Date: November 17
th
, 2024
The Minister of Communications and Information Technology Amr Talaat has attended the graduation ceremony of the Cybersecurity Academy for Juniors and Youth program’s first cohort, at the National Telecommunication Institute (NTI) headquarters in Smart Village.
Launched in August in collaboration between NTI and the Egyptian Computer Emergency Readiness Team (EG-CERT) of the National Telecom Regulatory Authority (NTRA), the program aims to raise community awareness about safe Internet usage by providing training in cybersecurity skills and fundamentals, including methods to prevent cyber-attacks and protect privacy and data. The program offers free training to youth from various age groups, ranging from 12-year-olds to university students and graduates from different academic disciplines and universities across Egypt.
The ceremony was attended by the Vice ICT Minister for Institutional Development Ghada Labib, NTRA President Mohamed Shamroukh, and the CEO of the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA) Ahmed Elzaher, along with officials from the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) and NTRA.
In his speech during the ceremony, the ICT Minister emphasized that the training program has focused on cybersecurity given its significance as one of the most vital fields within the ICT sector. He underscored the importance of fostering early awareness of the necessity to protect data, ensuring it is shared only with trusted entities, and adopting effective methods to protect against cyber threats.
Talaat pointed out that Artificial Intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity share a key commonality: data. AI systems, he explained, rely on vast amounts of data to function effectively, necessitating data protection. Data has emerged as the new natural resource for nations, societies, and individuals, Talaat remarked. He highlighted that prioritizing cybersecurity reflects societies’ ability to embrace different technologies while safeguarding data.
The ICT Minister underlined that the training program, tailored to various age groups, marks the beginning of a broader focus on the importance of cybersecurity. He mentioned that the next year’s plan involves increasing the number of trainees, extending the training duration, and diving deeper into this field.
For his part, NTI Director Ahmed Khattab reviewed the key outcomes of the program, which trained and qualified approximately 1,496 students and graduates from 13 governorates. Participants included 549 students from 327 schools, 654 undergraduates from 41 universities and 46 academies and institutes, and 293 graduates from 61 different specializations.
Carried out in three phases, the program equipped students with essential technical skills in cybersecurity, enabling them to protect themselves and their data in the digital world, Khattab underscored. He highlighted that the training covered specialized topics, including securing social media accounts, avoiding risks associated with public Wi-Fi networks, addressing cyber harassment, understanding social engineering techniques, enhancing online safety, and securing QR codes. The program also featured practical elements through a boot camp, where comprehensive awareness activities on cybersecurity were organized, and hands-on projects were presented at the end of each phase to reinforce soft skills and improve knowledge retention.
Furthermore, NTI Director mentioned that the Institute has developed rich, informative training materials and resources, tailored specifically to meet the needs of youth. This is in addition to providing interactive activities and VR-powered games, designed to raise cybersecurity awareness and implemented for the first time in Egypt. He pointed out that NTI is expanding training hubs across various governorates through Creativa Innovation Hubs, with ongoing support from specialized companies to qualify future academy graduates.
It is worth noting that the program also featured practical activities aimed at providing a comprehensive understanding of cybersecurity. At the end of each phase, students showcased practical projects designed to hone their soft skills and apply the acquired knowledge. Moreover, an awareness session was organized to educate parents and guardians about the potential cyber risks their children may face.
The Academy’s first phase outcomes for trainees aged 12-17 include advanced training scheduled for the upcoming mid-year vacation, supplemented by supportive educational resources and the development of communication and presentation skills. Furthermore, 15 participants aged 12-15 embarked on a four-month Python programming course, culminating in cybersecurity-related graduation projects.
Around 70 trainees received training on real projects in partnership with CyberX, the Academy’s sponsor. Three outstanding trainees will be selected for employment at the company. In addition, approximately 50 graduates have been enrolled in the Egyptian Talents Academy (ETA), supported by MCIT in collaboration with Huawei Egypt. They will receive advanced, specialized training and be certified as cybersecurity specialists.
The Academy’s program has included age-specific competitions and sessions led by experts from NTRA, NTI, CyberX—a cybersecurity awareness leader—and BARQ Systems, a provider of cybersecurity and IT infrastructure solutions.
